facts.text: Aleatory uncertainty is natural randomness that additional study cannot remove; epistemic uncertainty is lack of knowledge that more data or a better model could reduce. The two must be tracked separately.
facts.quote: Aleatory uncertainty is natural randomness that no amount of study removes; epistemic uncertainty is lack of knowledge that more data or a better model could reduce, and the two must be tracked separately.

facts.text: In the braking program, aleatory uncertainty includes run-to-run variation in dust density, rain rate, target reflectivity, tire grip and brake temperature.
facts.quote: aleatory uncertainty includes run-to-run variation in dust density, rain rate, target reflectivity, tire grip and brake temperature.

facts.text: Running the braking simulation repeatedly with uncertain inputs drawn from their distributions estimates how the outcome varies.
facts.quote: Running the simulation many times with those inputs drawn from their distributions estimates how the outcome varies.

facts.text: Epistemic uncertainty in the braking program includes unknown true surface friction, unknown exact sensor response in dense dust, and especially model-form uncertainty: error caused by a simplified model omitting some physics.
facts.quote: Epistemic uncertainty includes not knowing a surface's true friction, not knowing a sensor's exact response in dense dust, and above all model-form uncertainty: the error from the model being a simplification that leaves out some physics.

facts.text: Additional simulation runs do not reduce model-form uncertainty. Ten million simulated runs may estimate variability within the model very precisely while saying almost nothing about an omitted phenomenon.
facts.quote: More runs do nothing for model-form uncertainty. The booklet puts it starkly: ten million simulated runs may estimate variability within the model very precisely while saying almost nothing about an omitted phenomenon [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The area validation metric estimates model-form uncertainty from the gap between simulated and measured distributions.
facts.quote: The area validation metric estimates model-form uncertainty from the gap between simulated and measured distributions

facts.text: The area validation metric can over- or under-compensate when aleatory and epistemic uncertainty are mixed.
facts.quote: but can over- or under-compensate when the two kinds are mixed

facts.text: Plain mean and RMSE errors cannot accommodate both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty in stochastic radar detections.
facts.quote: plain mean and RMSE errors cannot accommodate both in stochastic radar detections [Chapters 6, 10].

facts.text: Even a hand-built virtual site carries epistemic risk because undocumented assumptions can become treated as truth.
facts.quote: Even a hand-built virtual site carries epistemic risk: undocumented assumptions can become "truth" [Chapter 5].

facts.text: The booklet asks the safety board to distinguish aleatory from epistemic uncertainty, as NASA and nuclear practice do.
facts.quote: The booklet asks the safety board to distinguish the two, as NASA and nuclear practice do

facts.text: The credibility of rare-event simulation results, such as a missed detection, depends on input-distribution validity and tail modeling rather than run count.
facts.quote: especially for rare events such as a missed detection, whose credibility depends on input-distribution validity and tail modeling rather than on run count [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The simulation specialist asks for proof that simulation results are not dominated by model uncertainty.
facts.quote: The simulation specialist asks for proof that results are not dominated by model uncertainty [Chapter 13].
